ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-compliant KYC/CDD under PCMLTFA before issuance of any share certificate: verify each director, officer and UBO against government-issued ID, confirm 25% ownership threshold, and document source of funds/wealth. Automated screening is required against the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (Global Affairs Canada), Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act regulations, the OFAC SDN List, Foreign Sanctions Evaders List and Sectoral Sanctions List (mandatory for USD-denominated Swift LC and TT wire rails), the UN Security Council Consolidated List, and Interpol/domestic criminal records. The project tier is Low_Risk_Standard requiring standard CDD; any PEP nexus, including foreign PEPs under FINTRAC definitions, elevates the file to Enhanced Due Diligence with senior management approval and 24-month enhanced transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry — Online Registry (CORES: Corporate Registry Electronic System) and NUANS Name Search System, operated by Service Alberta, Government of Alberta (corporate-registry.gov.ab.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be in English and/or French using Latin-alphabet characters. Any non-Latin-script business brand must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet by a certified translator before a NUANS search. The ULC designation must appear in the name as 'Unlimited Liability Corporation', 'ULC', or the French variant 'Société à responsabilité illimitée' / 'SRI'. Distinctive element must be distinguishable from existing Alberta corporate and registered business names; phonetic and visual similarity triggers refusal regardless of spelling.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Banking, Trust, Trustco, Loan, Lender, Finance, Financial, Broker, Insurance, Assurance — require federal letters patent or Superintendent of Financial Institutions consent
Royal, Crown, Government, Ministry, Federal, Municipal, Official — require prior Crown or ministerial authority approval
Canada, Canadian — require federal approval or justification under extra-provincial registration rules
University, College, Institute, Academy — require Alberta Ministry of Advanced Education consent
Police, RCMP, Gendarmerie, Sheriff, Mounted Police — restricted and require law enforcement authority approval
Co-operative, Condominium, Acceptance, Guarantee, Saint or the name of any living individual — restricted or require consent documentation
Law, Barrister, Solicitor, Legal, Medical, Doctor, Dental, Engineer — require consent from the relevant Alberta professional regulator
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The NUANS name reservation is valid for 90 days; a renewal for a further 90-day period may be filed before expiry, but after lapse a fresh NUANS search and fee are required. Upon rejection, the incorporator may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of Corporations, Service Alberta, attaching the original NUANS report, evidence of prior ministerial consent for any sensitive token, a legal opinion on distinctiveness, and up to three alternate names. The Registrar must issue a fresh written decision. A further adverse decision may be appealed de novo to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta by originating application under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), and the applicant may simultaneously refile under a new NUANS report to avoid regulatory delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered-agent virtual office is permissible for the statutory registered office only when the provider is licensed in Alberta and maintains a physical street address capable of service of process, as required by the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). For the aseptic boba/tapioca pearl manufacturing project, a virtual office cannot establish Canadian commercial substance for CRA, CFIA, customs or banking purposes. The ULC must maintain a physical aseptic production and tubing facility in Alberta, hold the relevant CFIA Safe Food for Canadians Act license, and be registered for GST/HST with an operational address; commercial lenders and Swift LC issuing banks will require physical inspection of the plant before facility approval.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 85% probability of an unannounced Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) inspection within the first 12 months of operation of a licensed aseptic food manufacturing establishment; approximately 5% probability of a regulatory on-site AML/ATF examination by FINTRAC or the bank compliance team for a Low_Risk_Standard manufacturer using Swift LC and TT wire rails; and approximately 15% probability of a CRA pre-audit business visit to verify commercial substance, payroll source deductions and GST/HST registration compliance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 — s 6 (incorporation), s 9 (articles content), s 24 (registered office), s 43 (directors' powers), s 101 (first directors), ss 106-107 (officers); partnership treatment of ULC confirmed under provincial practice and Income Tax Act (Canada) s 248(1) pass-through eligibility.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Corporate Registry Division (online via Corporate Access; authorized service providers accepted)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed to obtain a Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA; no escrow or deposit requirement. Articles must state authorized share capital; a ULC may issue shares for nominal consideration provided the corporation remains solvent and the applicable solvency test is met.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: (1) the Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation of the Corporation, filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), are hereby ratified and accepted in their entirety; (2) the subscription for 100 Class A common shares by the founding shareholder is accepted, and such shares are issued as fully paid for nominal consideration; (3) the registered office is established at [Registered Office Address], City of Calgary, Province of Alberta, and [Registered Agent Name] is appointed as registered agent; (4) [President Name] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, and [Secretary Name] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer; (5) the directors are authorized to open corporate bank accounts, negotiate equipment leases, and execute all filings required for food-processing licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — NUANS preliminary name search (online Corporate Access portal or authorized filing agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS preliminary name search to confirm the proposed corporate name is distinctive and legally distinctive from existing Alberta entities. Verify the name includes the mandatory 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC' designation. Reserve the approved name for a 90-day period; note that a ULC name must clearly state its unlimited liability status to protect creditors.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search request form (with proposed name)
Written justification for any non-standard corporate designation
Declaration of unlimited liability exposure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for lack of distinctiveness, file a written reconsideration request with the Director of Corporate Registries within 60 days, or submit an amended alternative name for re-reservation without losing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and File Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporate Access online filing system (Service Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 Articles of Incorporation specifying: corporate name, registered office address in Alberta, share structure and authorized capital, unrestricted sub-class shares, unlimited liability clauses, restrictions (if any) on business or share transfers, number of directors (or minimum/maximum), and first directors. Execute the articles before subscribing incorporators, pay the statutory fee, and submit electronically through Corporate Access or a licensed service provider. The Certificate of Incorporation is issued once the articles are compliant.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Articles of Incorporation (executed)
NUANS preliminary name search report
Consent of registered office (Form 2 or landlord consent letter)
Consent to act as director for each first director
Filing fee remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected for deficiency, correct the specific articles defect (e.g., missing share class provisions, invalid director consent) and resubmit via Corporate Access; an additional filing fee applies for expedited review (24-hour service available).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office, Bylaws, and First Board Governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / Corporation's registered office in Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, hold the first organizational meeting of the directors. Adopt the corporate bylaws governing board composition, quorum, and indemnification; confirm the registered office address; appoint officers and the registered agent; approve share subscription and issuance; and adopt the corporate seal (if any). Ensure the registered office is a physical address in Alberta where statutory records are maintained and process- serving can be effected.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Organizational meeting minutes
First board resolution (covering registered office, officers, share issuance)
Bylaw No. 1 (general operating bylaw)
Consent of officers and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office is invalidated (e.g., non-physical address or landlord withdraws), file Form 4 Notice of Change of Registered Office with the Alberta Corporate Registry promptly; amend minutes retroactively in the corporate minute book to reflect the corrected address.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration (CRA Business Number)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO); Alberta Corporate Registry for provincial corporate tax accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register the ULC with the CRA via the Business Registration Online portal to obtain a federal Business Number (BN). Open the corporate income tax account, GST/HST account (mandatory if taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 annually), and payroll deduction account (if hiring employees). Since the ULC is resident in Alberta, also register for the Alberta corporate tax account and confirm no separate provincial incorporation registration is required for intra-Alberta activity. File the Alberta Annual Return through the registry.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Directors' full legal names, addresses, and social insurance numbers
Evidence of identity verification (business and directors)
Bank account details for CRA direct deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the BN application is rejected or held, contact CRA Business Inquiries (1-800-959-5525) to reconcile mismatched director data; reactivate a cancelled or suspended BN by filing the required tax returns and paying any arrears, then request reinstatement via CRA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Minute Book, Share Certificates, and Statutory Disclosure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation (internal records) / Alberta Corporate Registry (annual filing compliance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish the ULC's corporate minute book containing the Certificate of Incorporation, articles, bylaws, registers of directors and shareholders, share transfer ledger, and minutes of all meetings. Issue share certificates to the founding shareholder(s) reflecting the approved authorized capital. Record any post-incorporation unanimous shareholder agreement if intended to preserve unlimited liability pass-through status. Set a fiscal year-end and file the Alberta Annual Return (Corporate Registry) within the required annual cycle.
required_dossiers: Corporate minute book and statutory registers
Share certificates and share transfer ledger
Unanimous shareholder agreement (optional but recommended for ULC)
Alberta Annual Return form (filed electronically)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is flagged late or deficient, file a late Annual Return via Corporate Access and pay the reinstatement/late filing fee; correct register discrepancies with a directors' resolution and update the registry records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) — Food Safety Licensing Division; Alberta Agriculture and Irrigation — Food Safety and Inspection Branch (provincial co-regulator)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act (SFCA) Food Business Operating Licence — Category: Food Processing — Shelf-Stable (Canned/Aseptic) Tapioca Pearls; plus municipal food manufacturing facility permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 — Minor/Registration tier under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA): a canned-boba process line typically triggers a low-threshold environmental registration (potentially exempt if wastewater is fully sewered and boiler capacity is below the intensive air-emission threshold), with a full EIA Report required only if large-scale discharge or air emission limits are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharge to municipal sewer meeting pH 6.0-9.5, TSS < 350 mg/L, BOD5 surcharge applicable; surface discharge, if any, must comply with Alberta Surface Water Quality Guidelines. Air emissions: steam boiler NOx ≤ 420 mg/m³, PM ≤ 150 mg/m³ (Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives); VOCs minimal from starch-sugar processing — keep below 10 tonnes/yr reporting threshold. Waste handling: organic tapioca residue classified as non-hazardous, managed under the Alberta Waste Regulation (AR 192/1996) via composting or anaerobic digestion; no hazardous waste generation expected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire: Alberta Fire Code (SAFE) certificate and municipal fire marshal inspection for food-processing occupancy (Class F / Industrial), including sprinkler approval and emergency exit clearance. Structural load: engineering inspection of the aseptic retort/autoclave line for floor-load capacity and pressure-vessel registration under the Alberta Pressure Equipment Safety Regulation. Occupational: Alberta OHS Act workplace hazard clearance, WHMIS 2015 compliance, ergonomic and hot-surface safety audits, and Workers' Compensation Board (WCB-Alberta) coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including CRA My Business Account and the Business Registration Online service. Alberta administers provincial corporate income tax through the CRA under tax-collection agreements; Alberta corporate registry filings are separate from tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta unlimited liability corporation (ULC) must obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) and register the applicable program accounts, including a corporate income tax account (RC) and, when required, a GST/HST account (RT). Incorporation or registration in Alberta does not itself complete all CRA program-account registrations. Apply through CRA Business Registration Online where available or the CRA's prescribed non-resident or business registration process; provide the entity's legal name, Alberta registration particulars, registered and mailing addresses, incorporation documents, business activities, fiscal year-end, directors, and authorized representative information. A non-resident conducting business in Canada may also need a BN and GST/HST registration. GST/HST registration is generally required when the entity is not a small supplier or otherwise has a statutory registration obligation. CRA may require additional information or security from a non-resident registrant. The GST/HST account number is the BN followed by the RT program identifier and account reference.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Canadian ULC is generally a corporation and a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act (Canada); it is not a domestic pass-through entity. Canada has no general check-the-box election allowing a ULC to elect partnership or disregarded-entity treatment for Canadian tax purposes. A ULC may be treated as fiscally transparent under the domestic law of a foreign jurisdiction, including the United States, depending on its governing law and applicable elections there. That foreign classification does not change its Canadian corporate status and may produce hybrid-entity or treaty-eligibility issues. No general Canadian hybrid-mismatch election converts the ULC into a pass-through entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST); Alberta does not impose a provincial sales tax. GST/HST rules are federal, with the applicable rate depending on place-of-supply rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters, subject to the statutory small-supplier rules and exceptions. The threshold does not necessarily protect non-residents making taxable supplies in Canada; a non-resident carrying on business in Canada or otherwise required to register may have to register regardless of the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no general real-time GST invoice-clearance, mandatory tax-authority API, or digital-stamping regime for ordinary domestic business-to-business invoices. GST registrants must issue invoices or other supporting documentation meeting applicable Excise Tax Act requirements, retain adequate books and records, and file GST returns electronically when required. CRA electronic filing and payment obligations may apply according to registrant status and filing requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Qualifying goods supplied for export from Canada may be zero-rated where the statutory conditions are met, including applicable requirements that the recipient not take delivery in Canada and that the supplier retain evidence of export. A manufacturer exporting its own goods may make zero-rated export supplies, subject to the applicable rules and documentary substantiation. Services are not zero-rated merely because the customer or payment is offshore; eligibility depends on the specific exported-service provisions, recipient status, place of performance, and statutory exclusions. Zero-rating is distinct from exemption and generally preserves input tax credit entitlement for related GST expenses.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian export declaration or applicable electronic export reporting confirmation, where required
Commercial invoice and sales contract identifying the goods, foreign recipient, destination, and consideration
Carrier-issued bill of lading, air waybill, or other transport document
Proof of delivery or other reliable evidence that the goods were exported from Canada
Proof of payment or settlement records where relevant to substantiate the transaction
Inward Remittance Certificate: not a generally prescribed Canadian GST export-zero-rating document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no general foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. A registrant claiming zero-rating must retain records sufficient to establish that the statutory export conditions were met. CRA may deny zero-rating and assess GST, interest, and applicable penalties if the evidence is inadequate or the supply does not qualify. False statements or omissions may attract penalties under the Excise Tax Act, including gross-negligence penalties where applicable; deliberate tax evasion may also result in prosecution. Assessment periods and reassessment rules depend on the applicable statutory provisions and facts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return for the Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the incorporation anniversary date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: On-time fee CAD 50; a CAD 50 late surcharge applies after the anniversary filing deadline. If the annual return remains unfiled for one year, the Registrar may issue a notice of intent to strike off; continued default leads to administrative dissolution and loss of legal status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, a private ULC must appoint an auditor unless all shareholders consent to waive the audit requirement by unanimous resolution. A mandatory audit may additionally be triggered by reporting-issuer status, regulatory license conditions, or lender covenant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for non-public ULCs unless the corporation has made an IFRS selection.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta ULCs do not file a separate annual UBO report. Annual Return verifications cover registered office, directors, and financial year information only. Any shareholding transfer during the year must be recorded in the Register of Members, and the annual return must still be signed by a director, certifying that the Registry information is correct.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registered Office and Records Address Register

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small business deduction: combined 9% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income; SR&ED tax credits; Alberta Innovation Employment Grant (if applicable)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed via CRA My Business Account or electronic tax software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the fiscal year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Canadian-source revenue only; allocate based on permanent establishment
Deduct expenses directly related to Canadian-source revenue; apply arm's length pricing
Compute net income from Canadian operations; adjust for transfer pricing
Apply treaty provisions and deductions; ensure proper allocation
Calculate federal tax at 15% (or 9% if small business deduction applies)
Calculate Alberta tax at 8% (or 2% if small business deduction applies)
Sum of federal and provincial tax; remit with return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of balance owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months; repeated failure: additional penalties; interest accrues on unpaid amounts

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, the non-resident recipient must provide a valid Certificate of Residence (Form NR301 for dividends) to the payer before payment. The payer must withhold at the reduced treaty rate if the certificate is provided. For Canada-US treaty, portfolio dividends 15%, substantial shareholding 5%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: 25% for both royalties and interest. Treaty rates: royalties typically 10% (Canada-US), interest 10% (Canada-US) but may be 0% for arm's length under certain conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for transactions with non-residents; Master File and Local File required if group revenue exceeds CAD 50 million
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have a specific ESR, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and transfer pricing rules require economic substance. Transactions lacking commercial substance may be recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful evasion of tax, false statements, or omission of income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% of tax evaded, plus fines up to CAD 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years (Income Tax Act s. 238)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes under s. 227.1; civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment for fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a ULC as a shell to avoid tax without engaging in real business operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, penalties under GAAR, and criminal charges for tax evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for tax evasion if they knowingly participated in the scheme
